To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the glycerol-3-phosphate shuttle is the major pathway of reducing equivalent transport from cytoplasmic glycolysis into mitochondria in the Ehrlich ascite tumour cells.

the rate of reducing equivalent transfer between the cytosol and mitochondria is dependent upon the nature of the substrate and the presence of other substrates, and that the glycerol-3-phosphate and malate/aspartrate shuttles are both active.

Ehrlich ascite cells utilize two major redox shuttling systems to transfer reducing equivalents from the cytoplasm to the mitochondria, the malate/asparate shuttle and the glycerol-3-phosphate shuttle.

the role of the glycerolphosphate shuttle in the metabolism of Ehrlich ascite cells.
the elucidation of the metabolic pathways involved in the utilization of lactate by tumour cells, in particular the mechanisms of transfer of reducing power from cytosol to mitochondria.

the study of the metabolic pathways and enzymes that are involved in the regulation of the glycerophospholipid synthesis in mammalian cells, with particular attention to the role of the glycerokinase and phosphatidate phosphohydrolase reactions in the regulation of this process.

the glycerol-3-phosphate shuttle is the major shuttle for the transport of reducing equivalents from the cytoplasm to the mitochondria in Ehrlich Ascites tumour cells, although in the presence of a high glycolytic rate, the malate/asparate shuttle is also active.

Ehrlich ascite tumour cells have the capacity to use the glycerol-3-phosphate shuttle and/or the malate/asparate shuttle to transfer reducing equivalents from the cytosol into mitochondria, but only in the presence of added carbohydrate, and only if the glycerol phosphate shuttle is active, i.e. if glycolysis is occurring.

the glycerol-3-phosphate shuttle is a more efficient mechanism for the transfer of reducing equivalents between cytosol and mitochondria in hepatocytes and Ehrlich ascite tumour cells than the malate/asparate shuttle.

the glycerol-3-phosphate shuttle is a key player in the energy metabolism of Ehrlich ascitic tumor cells and is a potential target for cancer treatment.
